Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ It was said: (this refers to) the Qur'an. It is also possible to say: this is a reference to the passage ﴿The imminent (Hour) has drawn near﴾, for they used to wonder at the resurrection of bodies and the gathering of bones after they had decayed.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and laugh?﴾, it is possible that the meaning is "and you laugh at this discourse," as He said, the Exalted, concerning Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 47]. They also used to laugh at the discourse of the Prophet and the Qur'an. It is also possible that it is a denunciation of laughter in general while hearing the discourse of the Resurrection, meaning: do you laugh while you have heard that the Resurrection has drawn near? It would have been right for you not to laugh at that time.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and do not weep?﴾, that is: it would have been right for you to weep over it, so you would abandon that and do the opposite.

﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and you are sāmidūn﴾, that is: heedless. It is expressed in the form of the active participle because heedlessness is constant, whereas laughing and wondering are two matters that recur and cease.

﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship﴾ It is possible that the command is general. It is also possible that it is an iltifat (shift of address), so that it is as if He said: "O believers, prostrate in gratitude for the guidance and occupy yourselves with worship." He did not say "worship Allah" either because it is already known, or because worship in reality is only due to Allah. So He said: ﴿and worship﴾, meaning: carry out what is commanded, and do not worship other than Allah, for that is not worship. This fits the prostration upon its recitation with a fit that is stronger and more complete than if we take it in the general sense.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings upon our master Muhammad, the master of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, and upon all his family and companions.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ It was said: (this refers to) the Qur'an. It is also possible to say: this is a reference to the passage ﴿The imminent (Hour) has drawn near﴾, for they used to wonder at the resurrection of bodies and the gathering of bones after they had decayed.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and laugh?﴾, it is possible that the meaning is "and you laugh at this discourse," as He said, the Exalted, concerning Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿But when he brought them Our signs, behold, they laughed at them﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 47]. They also used to laugh at the discourse of the Prophet and the Qur'an. It is also possible that it is a denunciation of laughter in general while hearing the discourse of the Resurrection, meaning: do you laugh while you have heard that the Resurrection has drawn near? It would have been right for you not to laugh at that time.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and do not weep?﴾, that is: it would have been right for you to weep over it, so you would abandon that and do the opposite.

﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and you are sāmidūn﴾, that is: heedless. It is expressed in the form of the active participle because heedlessness is constant, whereas laughing and wondering are two matters that recur and cease.

﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship﴾ It is possible that the command is general. It is also possible that it is an iltifat (shift of address), so that it is as if He said: "O believers, prostrate in gratitude for the guidance and occupy yourselves with worship." He did not say "worship Allah" either because it is already known, or because worship in reality is only due to Allah. So He said: ﴿and worship﴾, meaning: carry out what is commanded, and do not worship other than Allah, for that is not worship. This fits the prostration upon its recitation with a fit that is stronger and more complete than if we take it in the general sense.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings upon our master Muhammad, the master of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, and upon all his family and companions.
